Area.evidence_source: The Asian immigrant patients with no history of suicide attempts shared a similar clinical profile with the repeated attempters in terms of nonadherence to treatment and repeated psychiatric hospitalizations... While persisting symptoms of mental illness, especially command auditory hallucinations, could increase patients' risks of suicidal ideation and behavior, interviews with persons who made repeated attempts indicated that the psychological and social impact of suffering from a mental illness was a more pervasive factor exacerbating their feelings of helplessness and hopelessness. Three major themes from the interviews, identified in at least 85% of the participants' narratives, illuminated the depth of their psychological pain associated with their struggles with mental illness.
